neighbours.label: epistemic judgement words: the verb or noun where a speaker judges what is true or works out a fact ('I don't think', 'to determine', 'as though', 'the correct answer'); the same frames with physical-action verbs stay low
fire: Frankly, I don't think the new rules will change much for small shops.
The engineers ran tests to determine whether the beam could carry the load.
From the window it seemed as though the whole street was asleep.
On the quiz, the correct answer was Lisbon, not Madrid.
Most voters, I suspect, think the debate changed nothing.
The detective tried to work out which guest was lying about the time.
My sister believes the shop is closed on Mondays, but I doubt it.
It is not correct to say that bats are blind.
quiet: Frankly, I don't drive the new car much except to small shops.
The engineers ran cables to connect the beam to the crane hook.
From the window we watched the whole street being swept.
On the quiz night, the prize was a trip to Lisbon.
Most voters, I suspect, walk to the polling station.
The detective tried to open the door of the guest room.
My sister paints the shop sign on Mondays, and I help her.
It is not easy to see bats flying at night.
